key_insight: Low-fidelity pretraining improves atomistic prediction accuracy and uncertainty ranking, but predictive variances remain poorly calibrated, especially under energy extrapolation.
engineering_relevance: Multi-fidelity training can improve uncertainty-guided data acquisition, but variance-based confidence estimates require separate calibration checks.
method: Train deep ensembles of mean-variance MACE models on ANI-1x.
Compare high-fidelity training from scratch with low-fidelity pretraining followed by high-fidelity fine-tuning.
Track aleatoric, epistemic, and total uncertainty during training and under distribution shifts.
evidence_signal: Across test sets including unseen molecular systems and higher-energy configurations, pretraining reduces prediction error and improves uncertainty ranking; fine-tuning also yields a more effective uncertainty-based acquisition function.
watch_item: High-fidelity optimization makes learned aleatoric variance overconfident on held-out data, so better uncertainty ranking should not be mistaken for reliable calibration.
paper_title: Multi-Fidelity Training Reshapes Uncertainty Decomposition in Atomistic Models
